as_told.title: The Collins Elite study UFOs as demonic

plain: The Collins Elite is said to be a group of evangelical Christians inside the US government who decided that UFOs were demonic and so worked to block research into them. Michels brings it up again and again. Once he credits it to Luis Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who ran a small office that studied unexplained aerial reports, and to Elizondo's 2024 book Imminent, calling the group one of the main "blockers" of UAP research (UAP being the government's newer word for UFOs). In other episodes Michels cites the writer Nick Redfern's book Final Events. He says the group studied the phenomenon in a programme called Stack Five at Wright airfield and came out believing "this is all demonic." He also says the group was "very embedded in the CIA," though in a talk with the writer Peter Levenda he calls it a "rumor" and asks what Levenda knows. A researcher named Jason Simosa, also working from Redfern's sources, adds that the programme was funded in 1952 through the CIA's Directorate of Plans, with about 12 people working on it full-time. The physicist Maaneli Derakhshani only says he has heard rumours of it. Every telling goes back to Elizondo or Redfern. If true, it would mean religious belief, not science, shaped what the government was allowed to learn.
